Instructions to Candidates
  • This university examination consists of two 60-minute sections totaling 36 questions (36 marks).
  • Part A (Questions 1–18) covers first-order separable/linear/exact ODEs, second-order linear homogeneous ODEs, Wronskian, undetermined coefficients, and variation of parameters.
  • Part B (Questions 19–36) covers Laplace transforms, Dirac delta/step forcing, linear systems & phase planes, power series/Frobenius, and RK4 numerical methods.

5 First-Order Differential Equations, Separable Equations & Existence Theory Foundational [1 mark]
Consider the separable differential equation dydx=2xy\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x}{y}dxdy​=y2x​ with the initial condition y(1)=2y(1) = 2y(1)=2. Find the value of y(3)y(3)y(3).
A. 444
B. 222 \sqrt{2}22​
C. 252 \sqrt{5}25​
D. 232 \sqrt{3}23​
Correct Answer: (C) — 252 \sqrt{5}25​
The differential equation is separable: ydy=2xdxy dy = 2x dxydy=2xdx.
Integrate both sides: ∫ydy=∫2xdx\int y dy = \int 2x dx∫ydy=∫2xdx.
This gives 12y2=x2+C\frac{1}{2}y^2 = x^2 + C21​y2=x2+C.
Use the initial condition y(1)=2y(1) = 2y(1)=2 to find C: 12(2)2=(1)2+C  ⟹  2=1+C  ⟹  C=1\frac{1}{2}(2)^2 = (1)^2 + C \implies 2 = 1 + C \implies C = 121​(2)2=(1)2+C⟹2=1+C⟹C=1.
So, the solution is 12y2=x2+1\frac{1}{2}y^2 = x^2 + 121​y2=x2+1, which means y2=2x2+2y^2 = 2x^2 + 2y2=2x2+2, and y=2x2+2y = \sqrt{2x^2 + 2}y=2x2+2​ (since y(1)=2>0y(1) = 2 > 0y(1)=2>0).
Now, find y(3)y(3)y(3): y(3)=2(3)2+2=2(9)+2=18+2=20=25y(3) = \sqrt{2(3)^2 + 2} = \sqrt{2(9) + 2} = \sqrt{18 + 2} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}y(3)=2(3)2+2​=2(9)+2​=18+2​=20​=25​.

13 Variation of Parameters, Wronskian Systems & Green's Kernel Standard [1 mark]
Consider the second-order linear nonhomogeneous differential equation y′′−y=sin⁡xy'' - y = \sin xy′′−y=sinx. If yp(x)=Acos⁡x+Bsin⁡xy_p(x) = A \cos x + B \sin xyp​(x)=Acosx+Bsinx is a particular solution, find the values of the constants AAA and BBB.
A. A=0,B=−12A = 0, B = -\frac{1}{2}A=0,B=−21​
B. A=−12,B=0A = -\frac{1}{2}, B = 0A=−21​,B=0
C. A=0,B=12A = 0, B = \frac{1}{2}A=0,B=21​
D. A=12,B=0A = \frac{1}{2}, B = 0A=21​,B=0
Correct Answer: (A) — A=0,B=−12A = 0, B = -\frac{1}{2}A=0,B=−21​
We are given the differential equation y′′−y=sin⁡xy'' - y = \sin xy′′−y=sinx and a proposed particular solution yp(x)=Acos⁡x+Bsin⁡xy_p(x) = A \cos x + B \sin xyp​(x)=Acosx+Bsinx. We need to find the derivatives of yp(x)y_p(x)yp​(x) and substitute them into the differential equation.

First derivative: yp′(x)=−Asin⁡x+Bcos⁡xy_p'(x) = -A \sin x + B \cos xyp′​(x)=−Asinx+Bcosx.
Second derivative: yp′′(x)=−Acos⁡x−Bsin⁡xy_p''(x) = -A \cos x - B \sin xyp′′​(x)=−Acosx−Bsinx.

Substitute these into the differential equation:
(−Acos⁡x−Bsin⁡x)−(Acos⁡x+Bsin⁡x)=sin⁡x(-A \cos x - B \sin x) - (A \cos x + B \sin x) = \sin x(−Acosx−Bsinx)−(Acosx+Bsinx)=sinx

Combine like terms:
(−A−A)cos⁡x+(−B−B)sin⁡x=sin⁡x(-A - A) \cos x + (-B - B) \sin x = \sin x(−A−A)cosx+(−B−B)sinx=sinx
−2Acos⁡x−2Bsin⁡x=sin⁡x-2A \cos x - 2B \sin x = \sin x−2Acosx−2Bsinx=sinx

For this equation to hold for all xxx, the coefficients of cos⁡x\cos xcosx and sin⁡x\sin xsinx on both sides must be equal.

Comparing coefficients of cos⁡x\cos xcosx: −2A=0-2A = 0−2A=0, which implies A=0A = 0A=0.

Comparing coefficients of sin⁡x\sin xsinx: −2B=1-2B = 1−2B=1, which implies B=−12B = -\frac{1}{2}B=−21​.

Therefore, the values of the constants are A=0A = 0A=0 and B=−12B = -\frac{1}{2}B=−21​.

In our equation, p(x)=−2p(x) = -2p(x)=−2. So, −∫p(x)dx=−∫(−2)dx=2x-\int p(x) dx = -\int (-2) dx = 2x−∫p(x)dx=−∫(−2)dx=2x. Therefore, W(y1,y2)(x)=Ce2xW(y_1, y_2)(x) = C e^{2x}W(y1​,y2​)(x)=Ce2x. \\

We are also given y1(x)=exy_1(x) = e^xy1​(x)=ex and y2(x)=kxexy_2(x) = kxe^xy2​(x)=kxex. \\

y1′(x)=exy_1'(x) = e^xy1′​(x)=ex \\
y2′(x)=ddx(kxex)=k(1⋅ex+x⋅ex)=kex(1+x)y_2'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}(kxe^x) = k(1 \cdot e^x + x \cdot e^x) = ke^x(1+x)y2′​(x)=dxd​(kxex)=k(1⋅ex+x⋅ex)=kex(1+x)
\\
Now, substitute into the Wronskian formula: \\
W(y1,y2)(x)=y1(x)y2′(x)−y1′(x)y2(x)W(y_1, y_2)(x) = y_1(x)y_2'(x) - y_1'(x)y_2(x)W(y1​,y2​)(x)=y1​(x)y2′​(x)−y1′​(x)y2​(x)
W(y1,y2)(x)=ex⋅[kex(1+x)]−ex⋅[kxex]W(y_1, y_2)(x) = e^x \cdot [ke^x(1+x)] - e^x \cdot [kxe^x]W(y1​,y2​)(x)=ex⋅[kex(1+x)]−ex⋅[kxex]
W(y1,y2)(x)=ke2x(1+x)−kxe2xW(y_1, y_2)(x) = ke^{2x}(1+x) - kxe^{2x}W(y1​,y2​)(x)=ke2x(1+x)−kxe2x
W(y1,y2)(x)=ke2x+kxe2x−kxe2xW(y_1, y_2)(x) = ke^{2x} + kxe^{2x} - kxe^{2x}W(y1​,y2​)(x)=ke2x+kxe2x−kxe2x
W(y1,y2)(x)=ke2xW(y_1, y_2)(x) = ke^{2x}W(y1​,y2​)(x)=ke2x
